source.note: Wages are May 2025 medians from the Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics program, as published in each Occupational Outlook Handbook profile. Employment and percent growth are the 2025–35 projections in those profiles. When a profile covers more than one occupation, payBasis names the wage series and outlookBasis names the series used for growth and employment. The handbook states that employment for all occupations is projected to grow 3 percent and that the median annual wage for all workers was $50,980 in May 2025. Profiles were checked against bls.gov/ooh in 2026.

careers.title: Frontend web developer
careers.summary: Web developers create and maintain websites. This match uses the web developers wage, inside the combined web developers and digital designers outlook.
careers.fitFocus: building interfaces people use
careers.trainingDetail: The handbook lists no additional on-the-job training category. Employers typically look for a bachelor's degree, and some hire people with a certificate plus a portfolio.
checklist: Build a small set of pages that show layout, accessibility, and interactive behavior.
Study the languages and tools used to implement interfaces, alongside the bachelor's-level path the handbook describes.
Ask employers whether a degree, a certificate, or a portfolio is the credential they hire for.
Open the Occupational Outlook Handbook profile linked here and confirm state licensing, certification, and local wage notes before you enroll or apply.

careers.title: Digital interface designer
careers.summary: Digital designers develop, create, and test website or interface layout, functions, and navigation. Pay is the web and digital interface designers median. Outlook is for the combined web profile.
careers.fitFocus: visual layout, usability, and interface craft
careers.trainingDetail: The combined profile lists a bachelor's degree as the typical entry education and no formal on-the-job training category.
checklist: Assemble an interface portfolio that shows layout, navigation, and usability choices.
Take coursework in design and front-end implementation consistent with a bachelor's path.
Practice explaining design decisions to developers and to people who will use the product.
Open the Occupational Outlook Handbook profile linked here and confirm state licensing, certification, and local wage notes before you enroll or apply.

careers.outlookBasis: Software developers, quality assurance analysts, and testers
careers.trainingDetail: Software developers typically need a bachelor's degree in computer and information technology or a related field. The handbook lists no separate on-the-job training category.
checklist: Take a bachelor's program in computing or a related field, with projects that store and move data.
Learn to design, test, and document a service, not only a single screen.
Look at the handbook section on applications and systems software so you can describe the work in employer language.
Open the Occupational Outlook Handbook profile linked here and confirm state licensing, certification, and local wage notes before you enroll or apply.

careers.title: Software quality assurance analyst

careers.outlookBasis: Software developers, quality assurance analysts, and testers
careers.trainingDetail: The combined profile lists a bachelor's degree and no additional on-the-job training category.
checklist: Learn to write test plans, record defects, and explain impact to developers.
Pair a bachelor's-level computing path with practice in both manual and automated checks.
Read the handbook duties for quality assurance analysts before you pick a course.

careers.title: DevOps engineer

careers.blsTitle: Software developers, quality assurance analysts, and testers
careers.outlookBasis: Software developers, quality assurance analysts, and testers
careers.trainingDetail: Use the software developer entry path: typically a bachelor's degree, with no separate handbook training category.
checklist: Follow the software developer preparation path, and add practice operating the systems you build.
Learn version control, automated tests, and how a change moves from a laptop to a running service.

careers.outlookBasis: Software developers, quality assurance analysts, and testers

checklist: Prepare as a software developer, then practice explaining technical tradeoffs to non-specialists.

If a posting asks for a graduate degree, treat that as an employer preference on top of the handbook's bachelor's entry point.

checklist: Plan on a master's degree in computer science or a related research field.
Get experience with a research project that states a question, a method, and a result.

careers.title: Firefighter
careers.summary: Firefighters control and put out fires and respond to other emergencies. Typical entry is a postsecondary nondegree award, often EMT training, plus long-term on-the-job training that includes a fire academy.
careers.fitFocus: emergency response, physical work, and teamwork
careers.trainingDetail: Most firefighters need emergency medical training and a fire academy. EMT certification requirements vary by locality. Training after hire is long-term.
checklist: Earn the emergency medical credential your target departments require.
Pass the written, physical, and interview process, then the fire academy.
Plan on long-term on-the-job training and shift schedules after you are hired.

careers.title: Security guard
careers.summary: Security guards protect property and people. Pay is the security guard median. Outlook covers security guards and gambling surveillance officers. A high school diploma is typical. Most states license guards, especially if they carry a firearm.
careers.fitFocus: observation, access control, and calm presence
careers.blsTitle: Security guards and gambling surveillance officers
careers.outlookBasis: Security guards and gambling surveillance officers
careers.trainingDetail: The quick facts say to see the profile for training. Guards typically need a high school diploma. States commonly require a license, and armed posts have extra rules. Employers provide on-the-job instruction.
checklist: Finish high school and apply to posts that train on site.
Complete your state's guard registration before you work, and extra steps if the post is armed.
Compare this slower-growth wage with public-safety roles that require an academy.
